observations.behavior: Adds a 100+ failed/errored test threshold to the CI setup break definition.
observations.code_quote: # A single failing test in a job is still a failure, and its re-run pass is still proof.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies that a CI setup break excludes every trial of the attempt, not only its failures: a run attempt whose tests errored in three or more jobs or for three or more owning teams, or a job attempt with 100 or more distinct failed or errored tests.

observations.code_quote: "description": "Pytest and Jest tests worth acting on now, from the per-test CI spans over a window (date_from default -7d, maximum 30 days), ranked by blast radius: master failures first, then how many distinct PRs the test broke. Use this for \"what is this failing test costing us\" and to pick quarantine candidates. It does not measure flake rates. This data sees the main Backend pytest and Frontend Jest suites; package-specific runners are not included. Evidence is counted per CI run, never per span or run attempt: one run fans a test across matrix legs, and re-run attempts re-test the same commit. classification is confirmed_flake only when one commit both failed and passed the test (same_commit_recovery_run_count > 0): a \"Re-run failed jobs\" attempt went green on the same commit, or an in-job pytest retry (tests hand-marked @pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=N)) recovered it. quarantined means a tolerated failure was recorded while the test was masked. suspected_regression means only failures were recorded, which is absence of proof, not proof of a real break: treat it as real until a recovery proves otherwise. A test qualifies on any same-commit recovery, any master/main failure, a quarantined failure, or failures on at least min_failed_prs distinct PRs (default 3). A CI setup break excludes every trial of the attempt, not only its failures: a run attempt whose tests errored in three or more jobs or for three or more owning teams, or a job attempt with 100 or more distinct failed or errored tests. Counts are absolute, never rates, because fast passing runs are not emitted. Use selector to run or quarantine the test with its runner; nodeid is only the stable grouping key.",
observations.posthog_connection: Adds a 100-test threshold for excluding CI setup breaks from the flaky-tests tool definition.

observations.code_quote: "description": "Per-owning-team rollup of the CI test surfaces each team owns, over a window (date_from default -14d, maximum 30 days). It reads the same per-run evidence as engineering-analytics-flaky-tests and means the same thing by flaky: flaky_test_count is owned tests one commit was seen both failing and passing in the window (a re-run attempt went green, or an in-job retry recovered it), regression_test_count is owned tests that failed with no such proof and still hit min_failed_prs distinct PRs or master, and failed_run_count, same_commit_recovery_run_count and quarantined_failed_run_count count distinct CI runs across the team's owned tests, so one run with many failing tests counts once. A CI setup break excludes every trial of the attempt, not only its failures: a run attempt whose tests errored in three or more jobs or for three or more owning teams, or a job attempt with 100 or more distinct failed or errored tests. Each has an equal-length previous-window twin (*_prior) for honest deltas. Use this for \"which team owns the flakiest surfaces right now\" and to route a flaky-test or CI Signal to its owning team. Ownership is stamped on the spans at CI emission time from the repo's ownership map (the distributed owners.yaml files); spans without a stamp aggregate under the literal team 'unowned' (a nonempty 'unowned' row means ownership gaps, not a real team), and a re-stamped test lands under its latest owner only. Each row also carries test_file_count (the daily owners.yaml census denominator, with a window-start twin) and merged_pr_count (merged PRs by the team's members, bots excluded); teams with census counts but no CI signal appear with zero signal counts and a null last_seen_at. Teams are organizational owners of code surfaces, never authors. Read all counts as absolute signal, never rates: fast passing runs are not emitted, so there is no honest denominator.",
observations.posthog_connection: Adds a 100-test threshold for excluding CI setup breaks from the team-ci-health tool definition.
